chunks: And hold fast to the rope of the Qur'an and seek its counsel [or: take counsel from it],
and regard its lawful as lawful and its unlawful as unlawful, and testify to the truth that has passed,
and take lesson from what has passed of the world for what remains of it,
for some of it resembles some other, and its end is to meet its beginning!
and the whole of it is to change and depart.

key_terms.حَبْلُ الْقُرْآنِ: the rope of the Qur'an (metaphor for firm adherence)

ai.seo_question: How should one interact with the Qur'an according to Imam Ali's advice to al-Harith al-Hamdani?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) instructs al-Harith to treat the Qur'an as a trusted advisor ('istansihuhu'), emphasizing not only legal compliance but also deep contemplation of its narrative wisdom. This advice highlights the Shia scholarly view of the Qur'an as both a legislative source and a mirror for understanding the cyclical nature of worldly affairs, where the end follows the pattern of the beginning.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Adhere to the rope of the Qur’ān and seek instructions from it.
Regard its lawful as lawful and its unlawful as unlawful. Testify the right that has been in the past.
Take lesson for the present condition of this world from the past (condition),
because its one phase resembles the other, and its end is to meet its beginning,
and the whole of it is to change and depart.
